controllingAuthority.summary: A certification of eligibility for expungement, requested from the Administrative Office of the Courts and produced with a Kentucky State Police eligibility determination. It is a prerequisite attachment to any conviction petition under KRS 431.073 or 431.078. It is not required for KRS 431.076 non-conviction petitions and not required for KRS 218A.275 or 218A.276 void-and-seal motions. The correct terminology is 'expungement certification' or 'certification of eligibility for expungement'; Kentucky does not use 'certificate of eligibility' in the statute.

controllingAuthority.summary: On petition, the court may expunge misdemeanor, violation and traffic infraction convictions, plus any misdemeanor, violation or traffic infraction charges that were dismissed or amended within the same criminal action. Relief is mandatory under KRS 431.078(1)(a) for a single offence or a series arising from a single incident, and discretionary under (1)(b) for a series not arising from a single incident. Kentucky uses expungement, not sealing, for this track.

tracks.legalName: Application to Vacate and Expunge Felony Conviction under KRS 431.073

controllingAuthority.summary: Kentucky vacates the judgment, dismisses the charges with prejudice, and then expunges. It is filed as a motion in the original criminal case, not as a new action. Four eligibility bases exist under KRS 431.073(1): (a) an enumerated Class D felony, (b) a series of enumerated Class D felonies arising from a single incident, (c) a full pardon, and (d) any other Class D felony or a pre-1975 offence punishable by not more than five years. Relief is discretionary; for (1)(d) applications the court must additionally find rehabilitation and no significant threat of recidivism.

exclusions: For the (1)(d) catch-all: KRS 189A.010 driving under the influence, KRS 508.032 assault in the fourth degree, KRS 519.055 impersonating a peace officer, abuse of public office, sex offences, offences committed against a child, and any offence that resulted in serious bodily injury or death.

units.label: Post-order fee compliance and the installment plan
units.description: Stage 3, and a genuine process obligation rather than an afterthought: the conviction is vacated and the charges dismissed on entry of the order, but the record is not expunged until the separate $250 expungement fee is paid in full. The court may set an installment plan with a compliance date no sooner than eighteen months out, and no applicant may be jailed for failure to complete it. AOC-496.5 issues on payment in full. Without this stage the participant will believe they are done when they are not.

tracks.legalName: Completed Pretrial Diversion, Dismissed-Diverted, under KRS 533.250 to 533.262
tracks.publicName: Clearing a case that ended in diversion

controllingAuthority.summary: Class C and Class D felony cases resolved through pretrial diversion are listed as 'dismissed-diverted' on successful completion of the diversion agreement. The designation is not itself a record-clearance mechanism: it produces a disposition that then feeds the non-conviction tracks. A dismissed-diverted disposition is not a criminal conviction, the person is not required to list it on any application for employment, licensure or otherwise unless required by federal law, and pretrial diversion records may not be introduced as evidence in any matter without the defendant's consent.

exclusions: Diversion eligibility itself is governed by KRS 533.250 and 533.251 and is upstream of this track.
